notes: The booklet gives only pictures; exact stud-to-stud contacts were inferred, so most joined edges use null ports and attach each piece to the main supporting piece below it.

Black base (steps 1-22): connections are modelled as a chain from the first plate; real overlaps with several plates underneath are simplified. Light-grey top-layer plates (steps 23-28) are attached to the nearest big black plates (b4 left, b14 centre, b21/b22 right).
Inventory 4211397 (light grey 2x2 plate, x4) is used 3 times as b12/b34/b40 plus once as the Campanile base tw0.

Part-id mapping of ambiguous inventory pieces: 407001 = 1x1 brick with side hole (step 37), 3200001 = 1x2 with two holes (step 37), 6058177 = 1x2 brick with two through holes (gables, third dome), 4558952 = 1x1 bracket brick with side stud (step 47).

Fix applied: in step 47 the arch window sits on the bracket brick's side stud by its underside (anti-stud), not by a pin, so that edge is now anti-stud/stud. In step 46 the windows' pins go into the through-holes of the 1x2 brick (pin/pin-hole), which is valid and kept.

The two Rialto and the two Bridge-of-Sighs arches are modelled as two parallel arches side by side; the central 1x4 arch (step 39) and two 1x3 arches (step 40) sit on the white 1x1/1x2 side-hole bricks of step 37.
The third (centre, tall) dome is built separately on page 80-82 and attached on step 48 to the middle brown brick bw5. The two side domes (pages 71-76) are one repeat with the second copy mirrored.

Tower layers are modelled as 7 pairs of grooved 1x2 bricks, an intermediate brown plate (after layer 4), white plates, two columns, a lion-printed brick and the green pyramid roof; the 14 grooved bricks are 1+1+2+2+2+2+2+2.
Customer-service and history pages contain no assembly steps and are ignored.
